findings.text: commit 2e550a8's subject `docs(crew-observability-truth): record the manifest-template landing under s12` names the literal plan slug and a section label, which this plan's own recording (comment c-20260915-the-refusal-fires-on-prose: 'commit messages must not name plan identifiers') flags as a dispatch-contract violation; the sibling code commit 8417c0f is clean, so the rule was only half applied. Minor — the record is a docs commit and the repo's own coordinator commits use the same style, but the stated contract is explicit.

record says 'four asserting files' where the gate cohort was five test files; all numeric claims (49 of 49, 4 new, 45 pre-existing) verify exactly, so this is a prose imprecision in the evidence record, not a numeric error.

the FENCE — TIME prose now names the four wait keys but is asserted by no test — only the MANIFEST block half is bound by test_worker_prompt_contract.py; a future edit that silently drops the keys from the fence prose regresses unguarded.

justifications.durability: The property is bound by four tests against the genuinely composed prompt (real TaskNode + compose_prompt), so a regression that reintroduces the one-line form, drops a wait field, or loses the waiting vocabulary fails the gate on the only side a worker ever sees. Two notes, neither a defect of this change: (1) the tests assert the block *offers* the wait keys, not that a status-waiting manifest round-trips through recovery.py's wait machinery — but that round trip is the reader-side node's scope by design; (2) the FENCE — TIME prose that names the four keys is fixed but asserted by nothing, so that half could regress unguarded — the block half is the durable anchor, the prose half is a manual fix.
justifications.evidence: Every claim was independently reproduced from the worktree. The reviewed range b5480ee..2e550a8 is exactly the two claimed commits (8417c0f fix + 2e550a8 docs) touching exactly the four declared paths with 165 insertions and 1 new file. The named gate `tests/test_worker_prompt_contract.py tests/test_crew_prompts.py tests/test_the_prompt_carries_the_contract.py tests/test_the_prompt_carries_the_evidence_contract.py tests/test_worker_wait_contract.py` passes 49/49 (4 new cases in the genuinely new test file, 45 pre-existing prompt-composition assertions), matching the record's '49 of 49, exit 0' to the number. The claimed 12 pre-existing failures in test_crew_orientation.py and test_gate_evidence.py reproduce at HEAD with identical ids, and git confirms those two modules are untouched by the reviewed commits, so the zero-added-failure claim holds. The archive record's '119 insertions over 2 files (1 source template, 1 new test)' matches commit 8417c0f exactly (+119/-3). The schema the template now matches is real: recovery.py declares WAITING_STATUS='waiting' inside NON_TERMINAL_MANIFEST_STATUSES and consumes all four wait fields (recovery.py:1015-1025), resumption.py:878 reads resume_brief.
justifications.fit: The change removes the exact harm §12 documents: the template no longer teaches the malformed one-line form or an incomplete wait declaration, and it matches a schema the reader genuinely enforces, so template and reader agree for the first time. The coordinated merge is handled correctly — the plan landed summary and the archive anchor both state that the reader half must not merge alone, and the plan's tracked row 'manifest template 8417c0f,2e550a8 review pending' confirms the hold is being followed. Small deductions: the archive record says 'the four asserting files' while the gate cohort was five files (all numeric claims — 49, 4 new, 45 pre-existing — are exact), and §12 now carries two separately-anchored landed summaries (reader half from 9a2f95e, template half from 8417c0f) that a reader must read closely to see neither alone ships the section.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The dispatched goal, stated in driving plan comment c-20260915-the-template-teaches-both-manifest-defects, was that the worker-prompt manifest block carry `waiting` in its offered status vocabulary plus the four wait fields, put commits and changed_paths on separate lines, and name the four keys in the time fence so the prose and the block stop disagreeing. All of it is delivered: reckon/crew/prompts.py:222 offers `status: waiting | complete | blocked | failed`, the four wait_condition/wait_probe/wait_terminal/resume_brief lines sit in the MANIFEST block, commits and changed_paths each start their own line with no semicolon join, and the FENCE — TIME prose was extended to name exactly those four keys. The record (2e550a8) states the holding condition rather than claiming more: the reader-side repair belongs to a separate node and must not merge alone. Nothing in the goal is missing or overclaimed.
justifications.scope_discipline: The four changed files are exactly the run's declared write_paths (reckon/crew/prompts.py, tests/test_worker_prompt_contract.py, and the two docs records) — nothing more, nothing out of scope; the reader-side repair (reports.py / test_manifest_parse_format) was correctly left to the sibling node and recorded as a holding condition rather than triaged. One deduction: commit 2e550a8's subject `docs(crew-observability-truth): …under s12` carries the literal plan slug and a section label, which this plan's own comment c-20260915-the-refusal-fires-on-prose records as a dispatch-contract violation ('commit messages must not name plan identifiers') applied to a peer node in the same section; the sibling commit 8417c0f is clean, so the rule is known and was only half applied.
